score_semantics: Source-contract confidence only; not parcel-result or numeric elevation accuracy.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Catalogues
verified_facts: The official catalogue indexes full-coverage LIDAR surveys of England
Related datasets include composite DTM products at multiple resolutions
The catalogue is published by the Environment Agency under the Open Government Licence
semantic_limits: The catalogue is metadata and does not contain parcel elevation samples
A catalogue hit must be bound to the exact downloaded raster and survey index
Absence of a catalogue resource on the summary page does not prove absence of survey coverage

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue metadata guidance
verified_facts: The official guidance directs users to downloadable index catalogues for all LIDAR products
The catalogues include details on the time of year in which data was collected
The guidance was updated on 5 February 2024
semantic_limits: Guidance does not identify the target parcel or raster tile by itself
Survey date and season metadata must be read from the selected coverage record
Metadata discovery does not replace byte-level download hashing

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 metadata specification
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 provides GEMINI metadata at national and per-tile level
Per-tile metadata distinguishes grid DTM and vector contour representations
The metadata identifies the 10km National Grid tile and INSPIRE elevation theme
semantic_limits: Metadata does not substitute for reading the grid or contour data
Tile identity must match the raster or contour file actually sampled
Vertical reference and flying-date fields must be retained with derived values

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 contour data specification
verified_facts: Contour data is supplied in GML with a per-tile metadata file
The metadata file includes information such as flying date
Spot heights are selected automatically from the highest mass point inside closed contours and rounded to zero decimal places
semantic_limits: Rounded spot heights cannot become primary parcel-scale min or max values
Contours and spot heights are secondary diagnostics rather than exact polygon raster samples
Automated spot-height selection may represent genuine depressions or generalized terrain

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 data structure
verified_facts: Grid heights are calculated at pixel centres
The raster construction has no overlapping tiles or common values along tile edges
Mean high and low water breaklines use tile-average values derived from local tide tables
semantic_limits: Tile-edge discontinuity checks must not invent shared boundary values
Coastal tile-average water heights are not parcel ground elevations
The 50m grid remains too coarse for primary parcel-scale height difference
